title: Analysis of Federated Graph Neural Networks for Predicting Nuclear Core Properties
abstract: arXiv:2611.32509v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Federated learning has grown in popularity owing to the increasing data privacy and safety concerns. It allows multiple parties to collaboratively train a model without exchanging their raw data. As an example of highly sensitive infrastructure of national importance, nuclear reactors benefit from this approach, where---while pooling multiple large datasets from different institutions could improve machine learning solutions---the confidentiality of the datasets is paramount. In this paper, we demonstrate that a graph neural network (GNN) outperforms the convolutional neural network (CNN) baseline in a federated setting for a use case concerning nuclear reactor core optimization. The GNN architecture is better suited for the nuclear reactor geometry as, unlike the CNN, it does not require padding the cylindrical core and does not assume translation invariance. The key finding of this work is that input representation is more important

translated_title: 用于预测核反应堆堆芯特性的联邦图神经网络分析
translated_abstract: 由于对数据隐私和安全性的日益关注，联邦学习变得越来越受欢迎。它允许多方在不交换原始数据的情况下协同训练模型。作为具有国家重要性的高度敏感基础设施的典型例子，核反应堆受益于这种方法——尽管汇集来自不同机构的大型数据集可以改进机器学习解决方案，但数据集的保密性至关重要。在本文中，我们证明了在核反应堆堆芯优化的应用场景中，图神经网络（GNN）在联邦学习设置下的表现优于卷积神经网络（CNN）基线。GNN架构更适合核反应堆的几何结构，因为与CNN不同，它不需要对圆柱形堆芯进行填充，也不假设平移不变性。这项工作的关键发现是输入表示更为重要……
tldr: 本文证明在联邦学习框架下，图神经网络因其无需填充且不假设平移不变性而更契合核反应堆圆柱形堆芯的几何结构，从而在堆芯优化任务中优于CNN基线。
en_tdlr: In a federated learning setting, graph neural networks outperform CNN baselines for nuclear reactor core optimization because their architecture naturally suits the cylindrical core geometry without requiring padding or assuming translation invariance.
